method: MIXED. P1 is AMH's Chronic pain topic, paraphrased, no passage stored: the drug choices for non-cancer, neuropathic and cancer pain. S1 is the OPEN RACGP AJGP article 'Reviewing long-term opioid use in patients experiencing chronic pain' (July 2025), quoted verbatim, and covers what AMH does not: the REVIEW of a patient already on long-term opioids, which is the commoner general-practice problem. The two are complementary and are used that way. ⚠️ THE TWO SOURCES DIFFER IN EMPHASIS ON TAPERING and that difference is recorded rather than merged: AMH sets a 90-day ceiling with planned tapering, while S1 warns that harms have been associated with tapering, particularly rapid reduction or cessation WITHOUT PATIENT CONSENT.

claims.claim: CHRONIC PAIN IS PAIN PERSISTING FOR MORE THAN 3 MONTHS, or persisting after healing is expected to be complete; it is often further classified into CANCER or NON-CANCER pain, and acute exacerbations of chronic pain may occur
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: THE AIM DIFFERS BY TYPE: symptom relief is the main aim in CANCER pain even if function is decreased, while MAINTAINING OR RESTORING FUNCTION is the main aim in NON-CANCER pain; both aim to improve quality of life
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Before starting analgesics, ESTABLISH THE PATIENT'S UNDERSTANDING of their pain and be CLEAR AND REALISTIC about expectations: EXPLAIN PAIN MAY NOT BE ELIMINATED, HOWEVER IMPROVED FUNCTIONING CAN OCCUR EVEN WITH PAIN PRESENT
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Discuss the benefits of a MULTIMODAL AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY approach, as it is usually MORE EFFECTIVE THAN A SINGLE STRATEGY, and encourage ACTIVE INVOLVEMENT
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: In chronic NON-CANCER pain, NON-DRUG TREATMENT SUCH AS EXERCISE THERAPY AND MINDFULNESS STRATEGIES IS PREFERRED, and drugs should be used ONLY as part of an integrated, multidisciplinary strategy to improve physical and social function
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: RESERVE OPIOIDS FOR PAIN UNRESPONSIVE TO OPTIMISED NON-DRUG AND NON-OPIOID DRUG TREATMENTS
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Consider involving a SPECIALIST PAIN TEAM, particularly for patients already taking opioids IN HIGH DOSES SUCH AS MORE THAN 50 mg MORPHINE EQUIVALENT DAILY, LONG TERM such as years, or DURING PREGNANCY
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: THERE IS LIMITED EVIDENCE THAT OPIOIDS IMPROVE QUALITY OF LIFE IN THE SHORT TERM; IN THE LONG TERM THE EVIDENCE IS WEAK AND THE RISK OF HARM IS CONSIDERABLE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH's example opioid trial in chronic non-cancer pain: continue non-drug and non-opioid treatment; AGREE ON CRITERIA such as function and quality of life for success or failure; TRIAL THE OPIOID OVER 4 TO 8 WEEKS reviewing efficacy EVERY 1 TO 2 WEEKS; establish the LOWEST EFFECTIVE DOSE, ensuring the patient understands improvement may not occur or initial effects may not last
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: If there is no benefit from an opioid trial, TAPER THE DOSE BEFORE STOPPING because of the risk of withdrawal symptoms; if continuing beyond the trial REVIEW WEEKLY, and TAPER AND STOP if no improvement is seen with escalating doses such as more than 50 mg morphine equivalent daily, or if adverse effects become unacceptable
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states that opioid TREATMENT SHOULD NOT LAST MORE THAN 90 DAYS, FOLLOWED BY PLANNED TAPERING
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For NEUROPATHIC pain, consider non-drug treatment such as exercise and use drugs as part of an integrated multidisciplinary strategy; AGREE ON CRITERIA for success or failure, ensure the patient understands improvement may not occur, START AT A LOW DOSE and gradually titrate to the lowest effective dose, and ASSESS BENEFIT AFTER 4 TO 8 WEEKS, ceasing or switching if there is no benefit or unacceptable adverse effects
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: TCAs such as amitriptyline, ANTISEIZURE DRUGS such as gabapentin and pregabalin, and SNRIs such as duloxetine are the DRUG TREATMENTS OF CHOICE for neuropathic pain -- HOWEVER EFFICACY STUDIES ARE SHORT-TERM, UP TO 16 WEEKS, AND PROVIDE NO EVIDENCE OF CLINICAL SUPERIORITY FOR AN INDIVIDUAL DRUG; comparative studies are limited and long-term data are lacking
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: PATIENTS WHO FAIL TO RESPOND TO ONE NEUROPATHIC PAIN DRUG MAY RESPOND TO ANOTHER, EVEN FROM WITHIN THE SAME DRUG CLASS; specialists may combine drugs from different classes but EVIDENCE FOR COMBINATION EFFICACY IS LACKING
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ADDITIVE TOXICITY INCLUDING DEATH CAN OCCUR WITH CERTAIN DRUG COMBINATIONS, FOR EXAMPLE OPIOIDS AND PREGABALIN; use lowest effective doses and monitor closely
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Among antidepressants for neuropathic pain, TCAs and PARTICULARLY AMITRIPTYLINE have the most evidence of efficacy and all appear similarly effective; although evidence for DULOXETINE is limited to painful diabetic neuropathy IT CAN BE CONSIDERED FIRST LINE REGARDLESS OF UNDERLYING DISORDER; evidence is conflicting and limited for venlafaxine and SSRIs
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: PREGABALIN AND GABAPENTIN APPEAR TO HAVE SIMILAR EFFICACY, BUT MOST PEOPLE WILL NOT ACHIEVE EFFECTIVE PAIN RELIEF, ADVERSE EFFECTS ARE FREQUENT, AND THERE IS A RISK OF MISUSE, DEPENDENCE AND WITHDRAWAL
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Data are limited and conflicting for other antiseizure drugs in neuropathic pain such as valproate, oxcarbazepine, lamotrigine and topiramate; CARBAMAZEPINE IS CONSIDERED THE DRUG OF CHOICE FOR TRIGEMINAL NEURALGIA
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: In neuropathic pain, OPIOIDS SHOULD ONLY BE CONSIDERED AS A LAST OPTION AND USED SHORT TERM ONLY, though they may be effective particularly in peripheral pain syndromes; TOPICAL LIDOCAINE OR CAPSAICIN may be beneficial for LOCALISED neuropathic pain
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: CANCER PAIN can be controlled using the WHO analgesic ladder in APPROXIMATELY 80% OF PATIENTS; for the remainder, adjuvant agents such as antidepressants, antiseizure drugs, local anaesthetics, clonidine and ketamine, and/or non-drug treatments, are required
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: NO PAIN IS PREDICTABLY UNRESPONSIVE TO OPIOIDS: ALL PATIENTS WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE CANCER PAIN SHOULD TRY OPIOID ANALGESIA
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Analgesia and adverse effects may sometimes be improved by CHANGING THE OPIOID, though specialist advice is recommended; once adequate control is achieved with conventional release products, consider conversion to a CONTROLLED RELEASE product
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For METASTATIC BONE PAIN, RADIOTHERAPY combined with analgesics particularly NSAIDs is effective; BISPHOSPHONATES may reduce bone pain and skeletal-related events and should be considered for refractory bone pain; corticosteroids are occasionally used for intractable pain; and RADIOACTIVE STRONTIUM-89 may be considered for pain from widespread bone metastases from prostatic or breast cancer
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For pain due to INFLAMMATION AND OEDEMA IN CONFINED SPACES -- raised intracranial pressure, hepatic capsular pain, nerve compression or infiltration -- consider a trial of DEXAMETHASONE, noting HIGH DOSES MAY BE REQUIRED
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: BREAKTHROUGH PAIN occurs spontaneously or due to a trigger BETWEEN doses of regular analgesia and is managed primarily with SHORT-ACTING oral or buccal/sublingual opioids; onset of effect is APPROXIMATELY 30 MINUTES FOR ORAL MORPHINE LIQUID and WITHIN 15 MINUTES FOR A FENTANYL LOZENGE OR TABLET, which have more rapid onset and offset
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: IT IS IMPORTANT TO DISTINGUISH BETWEEN BREAKTHROUGH PAIN AND END-OF-DOSE FAILURE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: INCIDENT PAIN occurs on or is exacerbated by movement and can be difficult to manage because the analgesia needed for control causes unacceptable adverse effects at rest; when predictable, such as bathing or dressing, the options are a SHORT-ACTING OPIOID HALF AN HOUR BEFORE the activity, an NSAID HALF AN HOUR BEFORE, or NITROUS OXIDE AND OXYGEN just before or during movement
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Chronic pain' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/analgesics/drugs-pain-relief/chronic-pain, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
